title: Console minimum-viable: dashboards, tracing, and cost-breakdown scope realignment
creator: Sofia Patel
description:
Background: The Console Observability PRD called for a broad set of features (rich dashboards, full-span tracing, and token-level cost breakdowns). Given limited frontend engineering capacity and the need to ship a usable surface for customers within the next quarter, we are intentionally narrowing scope to a minimum viable experience that still delivers the core value: quick operational insight into latency, errors, and cost hotspots.

Problem statement: Full fidelity tracing and per-token billing views are high effort and low ROI for the first release. If we attempt everything we risk missing the delivery window and creating a fragmented beta experience. We need a focused set of features that provide immediate value to customers and enable rapid iteration based on real usage.

Goal: Ship a compact Console Observability MVP that surfaces: (1) per-route latency and error rate dashboards, (2) a limited tracing view sufficient for request-level investigation (sampled traces, top-level spans), and (3) aggregated cost breakdowns by route and model family. This ticket documents scope cuts, rationale, acceptance criteria, and rollout plan for that realignment.
acceptance_criteria: A1: Dashboard landing page with up to 4 configurable metric cards (Latency P50/P95, Error rate, Throughput) that default to the last 7 days and last 24 hours quick filters.
A2: Per-route detail page that shows time-series for latency and errors, with a pre-baked sample query, and a link to open the tracing pane for sampled traces.

A3: Tracing: sample-based traces available for < 1% of requests (configurable later) with top-level spans rendered (no deep span explorer). Trace retention for MVP = 48 hours in UI; longer retention kept in backend logs but not surfaced.
A4: Cost breakdown: aggregated cost by route and model-family for the selected time window (7d/30d). No per-token drilldown or per-customer chargeback view in MVP.
A5: Rollout: feature gated behind an opt-in flag; telemetry events emitted for every interaction (dashboard open, filter change, trace view) with schema documented in the PRD link.
A6: Performance: dashboard initial render under 1.2s for accounts with < 1k requests/day and under 2.5s for accounts with < 100k requests/day in staging environment.
A7: Docs: updated Console Observability quickstart (Drive link) and a short release note explaining missing functionality and the planned timelines for follow-ups.
A8: UX sanity: PM + Design signoff on the 4-card layout and trace pane prior to code freeze.
A9: No regressions: existing Console routes and auth flows unaffected; E2E smoke tests pass in pipeline.
A10: Security: no KMS or billing secrets exposed in UI; review by Security (ticket ENG-5145) marked resolved.
decisions: D1: Remove token-level cost drilldowns from MVP; show only aggregated cost by route and model-family.
D2: Limit tracing UI to sampled traces with top-level spans only; defer deep span exploration and performance flamegraphs to subsequent releases.
D3: Limit dashboard surface to 4 core cards instead of the originally planned 12+ widgets; allow later expansion via a card library.
D4: Default time ranges limited to 24h, 7d, 30d in MVP; custom date range to be added post-MVP.
D5: Gate launch behind an opt-in flag so we can gather telemetry and iterate before wide release.
D6: Defer third-party integrations (Datadog/Lightstep) for the initial launch; provide an export CSV for traces as a temporary workaround.
D7: Prioritize backend endpoints for aggregated metrics and cheap traces; deprioritize per-request cost attribution API.
D8: Connect the initial UI to existing runtime metrics (ENG-4921) rather than building a separate metrics pipeline.
D9: Acceptance benchmarks for performance and telemetry were agreed with Eng and SRE on 2026-03-02.
D10: UX pattern: card + expandable detail; clicking a point opens the per-route page and trace pane (no modal-based deep-dive).
open_questions: Q1: Is 48-hour trace visibility adequate for early customers testing long-running issues? (tentative answer: yes; reason: storage and UI complexity tradeoff)
Q2: Should the cost breakdown include model quantization bands (fp16/int8) for customers already on Dedicated? (TBD with Sales/CS)
Q3: What is the acceptable sample rate ceiling for traces in prod w.r.t. cost? Eng proposes 0.5% by default; PM suggests 0.1% for GA.
Q4: If customers ask for per-token billing on launch, what's the comms plan? (Design to prepare messaging)
Q5: Do we need an accessibility review prior to the opt-in preview? (Security recommended yes; timeline TBD)
Q6: Who owns the CSV export for traces: Console or Runtime team? (dependency: ENG-5007 decision pending)
Q7: Can the metrics endpoints handle bursty accounts during launch; SRE to confirm load test results (ENG-4921).
